angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 14,855,282 km at 101.52 pc = 1.96 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 43103: distance 101.523 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.062), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 101.523 +/- 6.294 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 9.4124 +/- 0.1621 mas (same row, RUWE 2.08), 58.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 21.353 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 43103: radius 21.353 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 256.838 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.08) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 14,855,282 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5004 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 43103: effective temperature 5004 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 43103: effective temperature 5004 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 517) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.4 from 2014AJ....147..137L; the 14 published values span log g 1.8 to 2.69, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014AJ....147..137L)
